summary:
The Little Flat-top Snail lived nowhere else on Earth but the flowing waters of the Coosa River in Alabama. Small and singular, this freshwater gastropod made its home in a river system that once supported remarkable biodiversity. Almost nothing is known of its daily life — its habits, its needs, the quiet rhythms of its existence — and now, nothing ever will be.

Beginning in 1914, the Coosa River was impounded repeatedly, its currents stilled into reservoirs. The Little Flat-top Snail was never seen again. By the time scientists formally documented its extinction in 2012, it had likely been gone for decades — erased not by time alone, but by transformation of the only place it ever called home.
